transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE); Lena Alvarez (Nexora, ML); Marcus D'Souza (Nexora, Platform); Priya R. (Nexora, Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on landing zone networking, credential handoff, and velocity to get benchmarking underway. Discussed staging access window, KV/prefix caching benchmark plan, KMS integration questions, and makeshift fallbacks for creds. Agreed on concrete owners and dates.

Topics:
- Staging VPC peering and CIDR
- Credential handoff, KMS/HSM path and RBAC
- Benchmarking plan: KV cache hits, throughput, p95 targets
- Hosted vs dedicated cost tradeoffs for initial pilot
- Telemetry/trace shipping and telemetry retention

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Um, quick roll call so we know who's here.
[00:07] Lena (Nexora): Hey, Lena here.
[00:09] Marcus (Nexora): Marcus here.
[00:10] Priya (Nexora): Priya on.
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood): Ethan here.
[00:14] Maya (Redwood): Great, cool. Quick agenda: landing zone status, creds/KMS, benchmarking plan, then next steps. I want to make sure we unblock the bench run tomorrow afternoon if possible.
[01:05] Marcus (Nexora): Yeah so on the peering, cloud team said they can open the slot this week but we need the staging CIDR and bastion details. We also prefer not to expose management plane so ideally VPC peering + restricted SGs.
[01:30] Ethan (Redwood): Totally, for peering we just need the CIDR and a route table entry, Redwood side we'll set up the endpoint-bound security group. We can also do private link if you want more isolation but that is a little more setup.
[01:50] Marcus (Nexora): PrivateLink might be heavier — for now we can take peering.
[02:10] Priya (Nexora): On creds, our compliance team wants the KMS flow documented. We prefer customer-managed KMS (CMK) and HSM-backed keys if available. Also need to see audit log retention and SSO mapping.
[02:35] Maya (Redwood): Understood. We support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS. For Private deployments you can bring an HSM; for Dedicated there's an option to integrate your KMS via cross-account grant. I'll send the KMS integration doc after the call.
[03:05] Lena (Nexora): Quick question — are there any specific RBAC features we should plan for at the start? We want to limit token scoping to staging team only.
[03:20] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, you can do token-scoped roles + per-route RBAC. There's also token expiration and rotation hooks. Our Console shows token-level usage, you can tie it to SSO group mapping (SAML).
[03:48] Priya (Nexora): SAML is the desired path. Can you confirm you support SAML 2.0 with group attribute mapping?
[03:58] Maya (Redwood): Yes, SAML 2.0 supported. We'll share a SAML metadata endpoint and sample attribute mapping.
[04:15] Marcus (Nexora): Back to bench — Lena, we probably need a few representative payloads. I can provide some synthetic traces but we should also capture a day of prod-ish traffic.
[04:30] Lena (Nexora): I can anonymize and drop PII, yes. I'll convert to tokenized prompt distribution and send by Thursday.
[05:02] Ethan (Redwood): Great. For the KV/prefix cache microbench, our recommended test matrix is: cold start baseline, 25% prefix hit, 50%, 75%, and 95% — at 200qps and then a 1k-request burst to measure p95.
[05:25] Maya (Redwood): Our SLO target for this POC was p95 under 300ms for chat-turns, correct? I remember discussion at kickoff.
[05:36] Lena (Nexora): We are aiming for p95 under 250ms at the pilot load. Cost is secondary but still important.
[05:45] Ethan (Redwood): Ok we'll try to get p95 numbers at varying quant profiles. Note quantization helps cost but can add +10-40ms depending on ops. Also sequence length distribution matters a lot.
[06:05] Priya (Nexora): Do you have any bench runs comparing 8-bit quant vs FP16 on your Dedicated infra? We need to understand accuracy/regression risk.
[06:20] Ethan (Redwood): We do internal regressions, but for pilot we can run a small eval set for your prompts. The plan: run dedicated node with int8 quant profile, measure latency and sampling score delta. We'll flag any hallucination regressions.
[06:45] Marcus (Nexora): How do fallbacks work if we see quality regressions — can we auto-roll back to FP16?
[06:53] Maya (Redwood): Yes, rollout policies support automatic fallback to a specified variant if quality or latency thresholds are breached. We'll configure a canary, and if eval metrics drop beyond guardrails, traffic shifts automatically.
[07:15] Lena (Nexora): Good. On telemetry — our observability team wants traces in Datadog and raw telemetry export to an S3 bucket. Is that straightforward?
[07:30] Ethan (Redwood): We can stream traces to Datadog and export token-level cost traces to S3 for retention. For PII you can apply pseudonymization hooks before export. There's also a telemetry retention setting in Console.
[07:55] Priya (Nexora): What's the retention default? And can we set the retention to 90 days?
[08:05] Maya (Redwood): Defaults are 30 days for deep traces, 365 days for aggregated metrics (enterprise). We can set 90 days for your pilot under an agreement. I'll note that.
[08:28] Marcus (Nexora): For the peering window — we can do Tue/Thu 10–12 UTC this week. Which is better for Redwood?
[08:36] Ethan (Redwood): We can aim for Thu 10 UTC. That gives us time to digest the CIDR and bastion details.
[09:00] Maya (Redwood): Action: Marcus to share CIDR and jump host details.
[09:12] Marcus (Nexora): Will do.
[09:25] Lena (Nexora): On credentials handoff, we want ephemeral tokens and least privilege. Can Redwood integrate with our Vault for short-lived certs?
[09:38] Ethan (Redwood): Yes, we can integrate with Vault for short-lived tokens; there is a Vault connector that issues scoped tokens for the Redwood gateway. We'll include connector steps in the doc.
[10:00] Maya (Redwood): Ok, now the benchmarking cadence — we propose first microbench tomorrow in staging (synthetic traces), then a longer 4-hour soak next week with mixed traffic.
[10:15] Lena (Nexora): Tomorrow works if peering is done; if not we'll do local synthetic with reduced fidelity.
[10:25] Ethan (Redwood): For timing: if peering is Thursday at 10 UTC, the microbench can run immediately after and we'll send CSVs. Expect columns: req_id, seq_len, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, kv_prefix_hit.
[10:45] Priya (Nexora): On encryption: is data at rest AES-256? And are logs sanitized by default?
[10:55] Maya (Redwood): Yes AES-256 at rest. Logs go through a configurable scrubber; PII redaction is configurable. We'll share the security checklist.
[11:15] Marcus (Nexora): One more ask — can we limit outbound egress from the staging cluster to a set of whitelisted domains?
[11:25] Ethan (Redwood): Yes the runtime runs inside your VPC and respects egress rules you define; we can suggest a minimal whitelist for OS package updates and telemetry endpoints.
[11:40] Lena (Nexora): About cost — do you have a quick delta for starting hosted vs spinning up dedicated reserved for the pilot?
[11:48] Maya (Redwood): Very rough: hosted is lower start-up ops but higher per-token at scale. Dedicated reserved gives ~30–45% unit cost savings depending on utilization and quantization level. I'll put numbers in the pricing spreadsheet.
[12:10] Priya (Nexora): Any compliance artifacts we need to review before we enable access? SOC 2 report, architecture diagram, data flow.
[12:20] Maya (Redwood): We'll send SOC 2, ISO summary, and a short architecture diagram. For KMS/HSM specifics, we'll include sequence diagrams.
[12:48] Marcus (Nexora): Ok that covers most things. Marcus to coordinate peering slot.
[12:55] Maya (Redwood): Recap: Redwood to share pricing + KMS doc + SAML mapping + example bench CSV columns. Nexora to share CIDR, jump host, anonymized request profile. Bench to run after peering on Thu 10 UTC if possible.
[13:12] Lena (Nexora): Sounds good.
[13:20] Priya (Nexora): Thanks all.
[13:25] Ethan (Redwood): Quick note — I'll also add a small eval run against your top-10 prompts to flag quality deltas pre-quantization.
[13:40] Maya (Redwood): Great, we'll follow up via email and slack channel. Thanks everyone.

Questions (raised during call):
- Can Redwood integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM? (Yes, details to be provided)
- Is SAML 2.0 group mapping supported? (Yes)
- Can KV cache benchmarks be run with different hit rates? (Yes, test matrix provided)

References mentioned:
- Redwood KMS integration doc (link to be shared)
- Pilot pricing spreadsheet (will be shared by Maya)
- KV-cache bench template CSV (to be produced by Ethan)

End of transcript.
